title: Iontophoresis (electrophoresis)
what: A weak electric current helps medicine pass through the skin to the right spot. Damp pads with electrodes are placed on your body.
why: For joint and back pain, after injuries, or for inflammation, as part of treatment your doctor prescribes. It is also used for children.
duration: a session usually takes 10 to 20 minutes; a course is usually about 10 sessions. Your doctor will decide how many
tell_doctor: If you have a pacemaker or metal in that area
Wounds, a rash, or scrapes on the skin in that area

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Skin should be clean, with no cream and no wounds.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not come hungry or right after a big meal.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that lets you uncover the area. Remove jewelry there.

bring: Your own medicine, if the clinic asked you to bring it
steps: Damp pads, sometimes with medicine, are placed on the skin
Electrodes go on top and are secured
The nurse turns on the device and slowly increases the current
You lie still until the end
The pads are removed, and the skin is wiped
feel: There should be no burning. Tell the nurse right away
after: Mild redness under the electrodes may remain. It passes on its own
Do not rub or wet the skin right after
Come to sessions on schedule. The full course matters
red_flags: A burn, blister, or strong redness on the skin: show your doctor

faq.a: No. Usually you only feel light tingling.
Yes, it is done for children too, if a doctor prescribes it. A weaker current is used.

reminders.text: Iontophoresis today. No cream on your skin. Bring your referral.
